description.value: The Hedley Public Library is a small branch of the Okanagan Regional Library, serving the historic gold-mining village of Hedley along Highway 3 in the southern Okanagan. Part of a 30-branch regional network established in 1936, the branch offers free public Wi-Fi to both members and visiting guests. A parking lot on the north side of the building provides access to this remote community stop along a popular cycling corridor.

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The ORL website confirms the address (789 Scott Avenue), phone (250-292-8259), and a parking lot on the north side of the building. Wi-Fi is explicitly confirmed as free for both members and guests per the 'Facilities & Services' section ('We have Wi-fi connectivity for both members of the library as well as guests who bring in their own wireless devices.'). No bike racks, washrooms, water refill, showers, or other cycling-specific amenities are mentioned on the website; the OSM name carries an 'ORL:' prefix not used on the website itself.
concerns: OSM name 'ORL: Hedley Public Library' uses an 'ORL:' prefix not reflected on the website, which refers to it as 'Hedley Library'.
No bike rack, washrooms, or water refill are documented anywhere on the website; only a general vehicle parking lot is confirmed.
This is a very small single-room branch library; cycling-specific amenities are entirely undocumented and may not exist.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: A legitimate public library with free guest Wi-Fi in a remote community on a popular cycling corridor, but no cycling-specific infrastructure (bike rack, washrooms, water) is documented and the branch operates with very limited availability. Recommend review to confirm whether access constraints and absent amenity documentation meet minimum WWC inclusion standards.
